title: The k-side target square under ambient projection
statement: Let A be finite commutative and d1,d2 supplied interchange diagrams for f:X→Y and g:Y→Z. Use the selected side n and the ambient geometry of [def-pur-etale-graph-product-ambient-geometry]. The rawSquare for the supplied k-square followed by the h-side ambientLambda equals sourceTransport whiskered by Ji_n Rq_n, then the associator, middleTail whiskered by the mixed source word RzH JE RR, and squareInterchange. This is an identity for the e/k and k/Q rectangles; it contains neither the f-side ambientLambda nor the inverse B exchange.

proof.text: Read the Cartesian, vertical, and horizontal laws of the chosen normalized exchange family from Classical.choose_spec of etaleProperOpenExchangeCube. The private normalized_cartesian, normalized_vertical, and normalized_horizontal lemmas preserve that exact family and include transport along equations of the proper and open composites.

In grid_core, paste the Cartesian k-side square above the supplied square, and the Q square above the Cartesian g-side square. Use R qG=qN r and productP prG=prH p to identify both outer commutative squares. Equate their vertical pasting formulas and cancel the inverse compositor on qN r. Horizontal pasting of the e-side and k-side squares expresses the Cartesian h-side exchange. Move the e-side exchange past the supplied square by naturality, substitute the vertical equation, and move the E K open compositor through the final proper compositors by naturality. This proves the core grid identity for an arbitrary coefficient object on H.U.

In full_grid, insert the inverse graph splitter and apply the final derived direct-image functor. Naturality of the supplied exchange and open compositor moves the graph splitter to the common source prefix. Naturality of the terminal proper compositors and the proved push_derived_assoc helper identify both terminal words with the compositor for (prH p),q. Replace the remaining core by grid_core. Specialize this generic component identity to each of the First and Second ambient geometries and use extensionality of natural transformations and isomorphisms. The original theorem signature is unchanged.

theorem etaleGraphAmbientSquarePasting
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z}
    (d₁ d₂ : EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram f g) (second : Bool) :
    (match second with
    | false =>
      let ah := EtaleGraphPresentation.ProductRow.ambientLambda
        d₁.compositePresentation d₂.compositePresentation false A
      (EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram.ProductRow.rawSquare A d₁ ≪≫ ah) =
      (Functor.isoWhiskerRight
          (EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram.ProductRow.First.sourceTransport d₁ d₂ A)
          (D((d₁.i)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]) ⋙
            R((d₁.q)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A])) ≪≫
        Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫
        Functor.isoWhiskerLeft _
          (EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram.ProductRow.First.middleTail d₁ d₂ A) ≪≫
        EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram.ProductRow.First.squareInterchange d₁ d₂ A)
    | true =>
      let ah := EtaleGraphPresentation.ProductRow.ambientLambda
        d₁.compositePresentation d₂.compositePresentation true A
      (EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram.ProductRow.rawSquare A d₂ ≪≫ ah) =
      (Functor.isoWhiskerRight
          (EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram.ProductRow.Second.sourceTransport d₁ d₂ A)
          (D((d₂.i)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]) ⋙
            R((d₂.q)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A])) ≪≫
        Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫
        Functor.isoWhiskerLeft _
          (EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram.ProductRow.Second.middleTail d₁ d₂ A) ≪≫
        EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram.ProductRow.Second.squareInterchange d₁ d₂ A))
